content: Lopinavir and ritonavir are prescribed in combination with other antiviral medications to treat human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) in patients with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). Lopinavir belongs to a class of drugs known as protease inhibitors, which work by slowing the spread of HIV in the body. Ritonavir is included in this combination to increase the levels of lopinavir in the body, enhancing its effectiveness. However, this medication is not a cure for HIV or AIDS and may not reduce the number of HIV-related illnesses. Additionally, it does not prevent the transmission of HIV to others. This medication is available as capsules and a liquid solution, both of which are taken orally. It is typically taken twice daily with food. It is important to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. Continue taking it even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Lopinavir and ritonavir may also be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about this, ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before starting this medication, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to lopinavir, ritonavir, or any other medications. Also, disclose all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking, as certain drugs may interact with lopinavir and ritonavir. These include, but are not limited to, anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), antifungals (e.g., itraconazole, ketoconazole), calcium-channel blockers (e.g., felodipine, nifedipine), cholesterol-lowering medications (e.g., atorvastatin, simvastatin), medications for irregular heartbeats (e.g., amiodarone, quinidine), seizure medications (e.g., carbamazepine, phenytoin), immunosuppressants (e.g., cyclosporine, tacrolimus), and other antiviral drugs. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. If you are taking didanosine, take it one hour before or two hours after lopinavir and ritonavir. Inform your doctor if you are using herbal products, especially those containing St. John’s wort. Additionally, let your doctor know if you have a history of pancreas disease, diabetes, liver disease, or hemophilia. Be aware that this medication may reduce the effectiveness of oral contraceptives, so discuss alternative birth control methods with your doctor. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Do not breastfeed while taking this medication. If you become pregnant while on this medication, contact your doctor immediately. The liquid form of this medication contains alcohol, which may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how the medication affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate the drowsiness caused by this medication. Additionally, be aware that your body fat may increase or redistribute to areas such as your breasts or upper back. Unless otherwise instructed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Lopinavir and ritonavir may cause side effects. Common side effects include diarrhea, weakness, heartburn, headache, difficulty sleeping, and rash. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, though uncommon, include upset stomach, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual bleeding or bruising, extreme tiredness, loss of appetite, pain in the upper right abdomen, yellowing of the skin or eyes, and flu-like symptoms. If you experience any of these, contact your doctor immediately. This medication may also cause high blood sugar. Symptoms of high blood sugar include thirst, dry mouth, tiredness, flushing, dry skin, frequent urination, loss of appetite, and trouble breathing. If you experience these symptoms, call your doctor immediately. Additionally, this medication may increase cholesterol and triglyceride levels in the blood. Report any unusual problems to your doctor while taking this medication. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. If stored in the refrigerator, capsules and liquid can be used until the expiration date on the label. If stored at room temperature, use them within two months. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as certain tests will be ordered to monitor your response to the medication. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
